$comment: Advisories at high or above that are allowed to stay in the dependency tree. scripts/audit.ts subtracts this list from `npm audit --audit-level=high`; docs/SECURITY.md is the process. Every entry needs a reason, a named owner, and an expiry, and the gate fails once an expiry passes, so nothing lives here by being forgotten.

exceptions.reason: No fixed release exists: the advisory range covers every postcss published so far, and every Next.js version depends on one. postcss runs only in the build, over our own stylesheets; the attack needs an attacker-supplied stylesheet or sourceMappingURL comment, and nothing in either flow (design 2.2, 2.3) lets a patient or a clinician contribute CSS. It is not in the server runtime and not in the client bundle.
Same package, same reach, same absence of a fix as advisory 1124252: a path traversal through a sourceMappingURL comment in a stylesheet we wrote ourselves.

Stack exhaustion when merging a recursive object graph. Reached only by the Prisma CLI merging prisma.config.ts during `prisma generate` and `prisma migrate`, which run on a developer's machine and in CI, never in the deployed app. The only fix npm offers is prisma 6.12.0, a downgrade past the migrations this repo already has.

Denial of service on a deeply nested glob pattern. Reached only by eslint expanding the file globs in eslint.config.mjs, which we wrote. Not in the deployed app. The only fix npm offers is eslint-config-next 14.2.35, which does not support Next 15.
